raw:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which organ is mostly made up of nerve tissue. The options are brain, liver, skin, and stomach. I remember that the brain is a major organ related to nerves, but I'm not entirely sure if it's the only one. Let me think about each option.

First, the brain. I know it's the control center of the body, with a lot of nerve cells. That makes sense because nerves are involved in sending signals throughout the body. So, the brain probably has a lot of nerve tissue.

Next, the liver. I don't recall the liver being mostly nerve tissue. The liver's main functions are related to digestion and filtering blood, so it's more about cells that aid in those processes. I don't think it's composed mostly of nerves.

Then there's the skin. The skin has epidermis and dermis layers, which are more about protection and sensing, but I don't think it's primarily nerve tissue. Maybe some parts have nerve endings, but not the majority.

Lastly, the stomach. The stomach is involved in digestion, with cells that produce acid and enzymes. It's more about the digestive system rather than nerve tissue.

So, putting it all together, the brain seems to be the organ that's mostly made up of nerve tissue. I'm pretty confident about this, but I should probably double-check to make sure I'm not missing anything.
</think>

1. Yes  
2. Reason: The brain is indeed the organ that consists mostly of nerve tissue, as it is the central processing center for the body's nervous system.
